title: Buffers
definition: A core Node.js class used to represent fixed-length sequences of bytes. It is Node's way of interacting with raw binary data.
simpleExplanation: JavaScript was designed for strings and numbers. It was never meant to read raw image data or video pixels (which are just 0s and 1s). A Buffer is a temporary storage area in memory explicitly designed to hold raw binary data coming from Streams or the File System before it is processed.
realWorldExample: If you use `fs.readFile('image.png')`, Node doesn't return a string. It returns a `<Buffer 89 50 4e 47 ... >`. These are the raw hexadecimal bytes of the image.

intermediate: What happens if you print a Buffer to the console without calling `.toString()` on it?
advanced: Can you resize a Buffer after it is created?

answers.question: What happens if you print a Buffer?
answers.answer: It prints an array of two-digit hexadecimal numbers: `<Buffer 48 65 6c 6c 6f>`. You must explicitly convert it using `.toString('utf-8')` to see human text.

answers.question: Can you resize it?
answers.answer: No. Buffers are fixed-size chunks of memory allocated outside the V8 JavaScript engine. Once created (e.g., `Buffer.alloc(10)`), it can only hold exactly 10 bytes forever.
